expectation: After preparing the submission I wanted to check whether a wider model search could beat the small utility model. Trees can learn interactions that the additive model misses, but with 200 households I expect a real risk of overfitting. Compare 17 fixed configurations using nested household validation, retain failures, and prefer simplicity within 0.002 inner log loss. No check outcomes or automatic prototype replacement.

inputs.data: visits.csv only; no household IDs or post-choice text as features
inputs.budget: 17 settings x 3 inner folds x 5 outer folds; no adaptive expansion
inputs.scope: Exploratory reused build folds; best among tried candidates, not a global best model.
inputs.prototype_policy: Do not replace or retune the frozen submission model.

outputs.limits: Nested folds limit selection bias within this experiment, but build data and outer folds were reused after earlier research. Family rankings and bootstrap intervals are exploratory. Tree models have no imposed own-price monotonicity or additive explanation guarantee. No new check set was used.
